error_handling.guide_position: set -euo pipefail plus explicit checks; guide states a failing command in a command substitution assigned to a variable DOES trigger -e in bash 4.4+
error_handling.best_practice: Explicit checks remain best practice; errexit is disabled by default inside command substitution for function invocations unless inherit_errexit (bash 4.4+) is set, per ShellCheck SC2311; guide also omits set -E/errtrace for ERR traps in functions
error_handling.evidence: ShellCheck SC2311 documents the suppressed-errexit case and the inherit_errexit fix; guide text overgeneralises the substitution case

bounded_work.guide_position: Named UPPER_SNAKE bounds for timeouts, bytes, retries, loop counts, find depth; timeout/PIPESTATUS discipline
bounded_work.best_practice: No official bash guidance contradicts bounded subprocess/input work; it remains the recognised hardening pattern
bounded_work.evidence: Guide rules align with bash manual semantics for timeout-adjacent coreutils use as described; no primary source fetched contradicts them

assertions_contracts.guide_position: Explicit [[ ... ]] || die guards for invariants and external validation; header/function contracts
assertions_contracts.best_practice: Bash has no native assert; explicit guards are the standard substitute
assertions_contracts.evidence: No primary source contradicts; guide correctly notes no optimizer strips shell guards

memory_ownership.guide_position: No ownership model; guide instead covers temp-file ownership, cleanup traps and subprocess reaping
memory_ownership.best_practice: Does not apply: bash has no memory-ownership system
memory_ownership.evidence: Aspect does not apply to a shell language; nearest analogue (resource cleanup) is covered under bounded_work/error_handling

formatting.guide_position: One formatter: shfmt, 4-space indent, -ci; SKILL and full guide disagree on -bn (see mechanical_fixes)
formatting.best_practice: shfmt remains the standard bash formatter; a single pinned flag set should be used consistently
formatting.evidence: Internal inconsistency is objective: SKILL.md gives shfmt -i 4 -ci, full guide gives shfmt -i 4 -ci -bn

static_analysis.guide_position: shellcheck zero warnings as a CI gate, justified suppressions only; bash-language-server for LSP
static_analysis.best_practice: ShellCheck remains actively maintained (0.11.0) and is the standard static analyser for bash/sh
static_analysis.evidence: Hackage lists ShellCheck 0.11.0 with the same stated goals the guide relies on

concurrency.guide_position: Track PIDs, wait for background jobs, bound job count; distinguish timeout 124
concurrency.best_practice: Still sound; note bash 5.3 changed wait -n / process-substitution job handling, which scripts relying on wait should re-check
concurrency.evidence: Bash 5.3 announce lists wait -n returning terminated process substitutions and related job-notification changes

testing.guide_position: bats for behaviour tests, half adversarial, hermetic mktemp dirs
testing.best_practice: bats-core remains the standard bash test framework; guide does not pin a version, so no stale pin
testing.evidence: No primary bats release was fetched in this pass, so no version claim is made; the practice itself is uncontradicted

toolchain_pins.guide_position: Targets bash 4.4+, prefer 5.x where available; no tool versions pinned in SKILL compatibility beyond tool names
toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current stable is bash 5.3 (Jul 2025); a 2026 guide should name 5.3 as the preferred baseline and re-check 5.3 changes (current-shell substitution, GLOBSORT, source -p, wait -n)
toolchain_pins.evidence: GNU announce and maintainer page both state current version is bash-5.3; guide never mentions 5.3 or its features

security.guide_position: No eval, no curl|bash, checksum verification, mktemp only, -- before user paths, env/PATH distrust, no secrets in argv
security.best_practice: Unchanged official/community best practice; ShellCheck SC2251/SC2311 family reinforces explicit status handling over blind errexit trust
security.evidence: Guide bans match ShellCheck-documented failure modes; no primary source contradicts the bans

mechanical_fixes.evidence: Full guide section 26 prescribes shfmt -i 4 -ci -bn; SKILL.md drops -bn, so the two files in the same skill prescribe different formatter invocations

mechanical_fixes.current: substitution assigned to a variable DOES trigger it in bash 4.4+
mechanical_fixes.correct: substitution does NOT reliably trigger it: bash disables errexit inside command substitution for function invocations by default; use shopt -s inherit_errexit (bash 4.4+) or check explicitly
mechanical_fixes.evidence: ShellCheck SC2311: bash implicitly disables set -e for a function invocation inside command substitution; fix is inherit_errexit or explicit set -e inside

proposals.proposal: Add shopt -s inherit_errexit and, where an ERR trap is used, set -E (errtrace) to the strict-mode discussion, with the SC2311 function-in-substitution example
proposals.evidence: SC2311 documents suppressed errexit in substitutions and the inherit_errexit remedy; guide currently omits both
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as an explicit, documented option in section 3, not a silent header change, because inherit_errexit changes function-call semantics

proposals.proposal: Re-baseline to bash 5.3 as preferred, keep 4.4 as minimum only if needed, and document 5.3 additions relevant to Tiger Style: ${ command; } current-shell substitution (no fork/pipe, REPLY form), GLOBSORT, source -p PATH, trap -P, BASH_TRAPSIG
proposals.evidence: GNU bash-5.3 announce lists all of these as new features; guide mentions none
proposals.recommendation: Adopt: document them in sections 2/10/20 with the same bound-and-check discipline; do not raise the hard minimum without a platform survey
